dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Cupboard, chair... all fixed.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: *sigh* I still need to go into town and pick up some materials...

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: First, though, I need to collect some wood. After all these repairs, there's basically nothing left...

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Huh? Am I running low on nails? I'd better head to town and buy some more...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you made up your mind yet?

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}, it's you. Are you asking about me joining the Frostmoon Scions, like Lauma invited me to?

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: If I'm being perfectly honest, I still haven't decided. The more I think about it, the more conflicted I get...

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: I came here to help them out as a way to say thanks for everything they did for me.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: But if my actions result in me joining them...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you, then.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Goodbye. You do what you need to do. I have my own work to get to.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hard work deserves to be rewarded.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: No, no, no. While I don't disagree in principle, I'm truly not after a reward.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Helping everyone out is all the reward I need. Now that the problem's solved, everyone's happy. That's enough for me.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Besides, I've made a little income, enough for a few extra drinks.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: But now... *sigh* I'm not even really sure what I'm conflicted about.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: I'm sorry. I'm not the sharpest knife in the drawer — otherwise, I'm sure I'd have come to a decision by now.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Forget about it, I'll come back to it later. For now, I need to build a workbench for Eveliina. Her statues are heavy, so I need to add some extra supports...

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: This'll do... Phew. Might as well make Granny Sarakka a new chair next time too...

choices.text: Pretty good repair work on this chair.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: Yeah, when I'm in town, I fix furniture for the whole neighborhood.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: *sigh* But this one's already gone through several rounds of repair. If it breaks again, I think I'll be forced to write it off.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: I also told Granny Sarakka that I could just make her a brand-new chair, but she insisted that it could still be used, and that we shouldn't waste resources.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: Then she had me use the spare materials to make tables and chairs for the children, and to help birds in the area repair their nests...

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: *sigh* Don't worry, that's just how she is. I'd never skimp on material when repairing chairs.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: Of course, I didn't do any different for those other tasks. You bet I repaired them all perfectly.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: Staying up late was tiring, of course, but it's nothing that can't be fixed by going into town to get maybe two drinks, before heading home to sleep.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, you don't live here?

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: Hahaha. Sorry, I forgot to mention it, but I'm not a Frostmoon Scion. I'm just... a normal townsperson, yes.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: I do owe them a favor for their help during certain circumstances I had, so...

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: When I arrived, I realized that my woodworking skills would come in handy, so that's what I've taken to do — doing some repair work to return said favor.

choices.text: So you've never thought about joining up for real?

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: Funny you should ask. Eveliina and Zirnytsia have both asked me to join the Scions and officially move in...

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: I gave it a night's worth of thought, but refused in the end.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did you have any concerns?

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: I'd be lying if I said "no"... Uh, don't misunderstand, it's not a problem with the Scions, but with me, kinda.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: Y'see, they worship the Moon Goddess, right? And they're real earnest about it, too.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: But as for me, I don't believe in her now, nor do I think I ever will...

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: And if you're wondering why, it's because I've never made a habit of believing in gods anyway.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: Granny Sarakka says that I could just live here as an ordinary resident, and that faith wasn't mandatory...

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: *sigh* But I don't think that's a good idea. I doubt I could afford affecting others by joining in that way.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: I'm doing this to repay the Scions for helping me. I wouldn't wanna cause them trouble instead.

choices.text: You're overthinking this a bit, I think.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: I know, but... *sigh* Like I said, it's a me problem — one I haven't been able to solve. For now, I'll just stick to sticking around and helping everyone out.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: Who knows? There might be a better opportunity to join in the future. I'll hop on the wagon then.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: If I had to be honest, this isn't a bad life. I help out here sometimes, and when there's nothing to do, I grab a drink in town and pass some time.

response.speaker: Wecksell
response.text: *cough*... I'm not sure what the Scions' rules are either. I don't know what I'd do if joining meant I could never drink another drop...

choices.text: The people here don't seem too uptight about that.
Sounds like you've done quite a lot of work.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The Frostmoon Scions' rules...)

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: (Wecksell frowns, seemingly troubled by his thoughts...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Perhaps someone who knows the Frostmoon Scions' rules can respond to his doubts...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Maybe <color=#FFCC33FF>Lauma</color> can help assuage his worries...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you...

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: If I had to be honest, this isn't a bad life. I help out here sometimes, and when there's nothing to do, I grab a drink in town and pass some time.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: *cough*... I'm not sure what the Scions' rules are either. I don't know what I'd do if joining meant I could never drink another drop...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Thank you for your hard work, Mr. Wecksell. Here is your fee for the repairs. Please, take it.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Oh my! When did you arrive, Miss Lauma? I didn't see you...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I heard the finches mention you while you were repairing Reetta's bookshelf.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: They said that you had to search for wood for a long time, and that they eventually had to guide you to a fallen tree.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Finches? Oh! I see. So that's why they were circling me. And there I thought they were looking for my help!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Ah, and they also said, "Thank you for the apple. It was delicious."

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Hehe, oh, that's quite alright. If anything, I should be thanking them for taking me to find the wood.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: If I hadn't found suitable wood back there, I'd have had to go back into town to buy some. At that point, who knows when Reetta's bookshelf was going to get fixed...

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: ...Hmm? Miss Lauma, isn't this a bit too much Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The extra is for the materials you purchased on your own.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry, that was just some scrap. I didn't purchase such major components that I need extra pay.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I must demur. You deserve this, so please, do take it.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: If you refuse, then I believe I shall have to ask my friends to stuff the Mora bag beneath your pillow.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: In that case, thank you. Oh, and — I believe you needed a new bookshelf in your library, yes? Just give me a few days, and you'll have it.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Thank you. That said, please don't overexert yourself. The library is meant to give everyone a place where they can relax.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: If those constructing said shelf were to be stretched beyond their limits, then the construction itself would be self-defeating.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Not to worry, I know my limits.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: On another note, Zirnytsia mentioned the offer she made to you. Should you wish to join us, rest assured that you need not worry about matters of faith.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: All of us are witness to the help you have rendered. We have long seen you as family.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Alright, Miss Lauma. I'll... give it some further thought.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: Thank you.
